style: Epic painterly dark fantasy card illustration, highly detailed, cinematic composition, dramatic rim lighting and deep shadows, a dark moody palette of charcoal, black and deep violet with small hot accents of light, painted texture like an oil painting.
race: Every figure is drawn as described in the scene; no other characters appear.
framing: Wide 16:9 landscape. The painted scene fills the whole picture edge to edge: its sky or background continues right up to the top edge, with open sky across the top quarter (never a flat colour band, blank strip, letterbox bar, border or frame). The main figure's head sits about 40% of the way down and a little to one side of centre, never at the very top; keep faces and key details away from the bottom centre of the picture. The painting runs right to the bottom edge with no emblem, seal, logo, line or border anywhere. No text, no lettering.

cards.companion_lancer: Kaelen, an Aureline lancer, the Captain's oldest friend, just broken free of a crystal prison. The Aureline, exactly as in the reference images: tall, slender, solemn beings with smooth pale grey alien skin, an elongated smooth bald head with one single large cyclopean eye that holds a starfield, a narrow lipless face, long thin fingers, a glowing golden halo ring floating around the head or neck, flowing ivory-white robes or gold-trimmed white-and-gold plate armour with fine gold embroidery. They carry sun-staffs (a twisted golden staff cradling a small blazing sun in a cage of golden rings) or sun-lances (long white-and-gold lances tipped with a leaf-shaped blade of solid golden light). Every Aureline is an individual: vary build, height, head shape, eye colour, robes, armour and markings. They are never human: no human faces, no noses, no hair or beards, never two eyes; even the old, the huge and the heavily armoured are unmistakably Aureline. Every single figure in the picture, background crowds and companions included, is an Aureline: there are no humans anywhere. He stands on the dark scorched hull of a battered human corvette drifting in deep space, shards of shattered violet-white crystal still falling away from his white-and-gold plate armour, a torn crimson cape streaming behind him, his sun-lance raised and blazing with golden light, his halo ring flickering back to life. Deep black-violet space behind, a faint nebula, sparks and crystal dust drifting; the gold of his lance is the brightest thing in the picture.
cards.companion_engineer: Mara Venn, a human ship's engineer, a wiry woman in her forties with close-cropped grey-streaked hair, a soot-smudged weathered face and welding goggles pushed up on her forehead, in a patched heavy work coat with rolled sleeves, a tool harness and a glowing amber shield-emitter strapped to one forearm. She kneels on the dark battered hull of a human corvette in deep space, one hand on an open hull panel spilling amber sparks and cool blue shield light, a heavy wrench in the other, looking up and off to one side with calm, tired resolve. Deep black-violet space, drifting embers, a faint blue shield shimmer over the hull.
cards.companion_defector: Vey'Sharr, a Xel'Naru defector: a being of living crystal, a figure made of separate hovering rose-violet crystal shards (no flesh, no skin, no cloth) held a finger's width apart around a single blazing core of white light in the chest, light leaking through every gap. It floats on the dark hull of a battered human corvette in deep space, one shard-built arm reshaped into a long crystal blade, a cracked and scarred shard where its old allegiance was torn away, a scrap of the human ship's charcoal cloth tied round its arm. Its head is a crown of sharp shards with one burning slit of light. Deep black-violet space, glittering crystal dust and embers drifting.
